html:
In 1797 the British shipped the defeated Garifuna of St Vincent, several thousand people, to the island of Roatan off Honduras. Many had already died of disease on the bare island of Balliceaux, where they were held after the Second Carib War.

From Roatan the survivors moved to the mainland. They spread along the coast of Honduras, Belize, Guatemala and Nicaragua, where their towns still stand.

The Garifuna kept their language, a mix of Arawakan and Carib with African, French and Spanish words, and their music and dance. UNESCO listed their culture in 2001. Each year Belize marks Garifuna Settlement Day, and many Garifuna today also live in New York.
